English Literature.question: ১) Who is the Father of English Sacred Songs?
English Literature.exp:
- Caedmon – ইংরেজি সাহিত্যের প্রথম কবি হিসেবে পরিচিত। Fathers of English Sacred Songs.
- Cynewulf known as The writer of Christ.
- Alfred the Great was a king who reigned England from 871 – 899 and encouraged education. He supervised the compilation of ‘The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle’, the earliest prose of English Literature. He is known as ‘The Law Governing’.
- Geoffrey Chaucer: Father of Modern English poetry.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ২) “Books, the children of the brain.” - is a famous quotation by -
English Literature.exp:
Some important quotations by Jonathan Swift:
- Books, the children of the brain. (A Tale of Tub)
- I cannot but conclude that the bulk of your. (A Tale of Tub)
- Undoubtedly, philosophers are in right when they tell us that nothing is great or little otherwise than by comparison. (Gulliver’s Travel)
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৩) What is a sonnet?
English Literature.option1: ক) A kind of short love poem
English Literature.option2: খ) A poem of fourteen lines
English Literature.option4: ঘ) A prose of special nature
English Literature.exp:
A poem of fourteen iambic pentameter lines is called sonnet. It is of three types: Petrarchan, Shakespearean, Spenserian.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪) An elegy is a -
English Literature.exp:
A lyric poem mourning for death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event is called elegy.
Gray’s “Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard”, Tennyson’s “In Memoriam” are two of the best elegies in English literature.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৫) A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action is called -
English Literature.exp:
A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action is called ballad. Ballad is mainly of two types:
1) The Folk and
2) The Literary Ballad.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৬) A literary attack through laughter and ridicule is called -
English Literature.exp:
Satire:
A literary attack on the follies and vices of an individual or a society with a view to correcting them through laughter and ridicule. It may be in prose or in verse.
It is of two kinds: formal (direct) and informal (indirect).
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৭) The Caroline Age belongs to -
English Literature.exp:
The Renaissance Period (1500 – 1660):
Preparation for Renaissance (1500 – 1558)
I) Elizabethan Period (1558 – 1603)
II) Jacobean Age (1603 – 1625)
III) Caroline Age (1625 – 1649)
IV) Commonwealth Period (1649 – 1660)
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৮) The Anglo-Saxon Period of English Literature refers to -
English Literature.exp:
The Anglo-Saxon Period or The Old English Period refers to 450 – 1066.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১০) The Neo-Classical Age of English Literature comprises ____ shorter ages.
English Literature.exp:
The Neo-Classical Age বা Pseudo-classical Age কে ৩ ভাগে ভাগ করা যায়।
A. The Restoration Age – (1660 – 1700).
B. The Augustan Age – (1700 – 1745).
C. The Age of Sensibility – (1745 – 1798).
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১১) ‘Fabian Society’ formed during -
English Literature.exp:
Fabian Society, socialist society founded in 1884 in London, having as its goal the establishment of a democratic socialist state in Great Britain.
The Fabians put their faith in evolutionary socialism rather than in revolution.

At the time of founding Fabian Society, Queen Victoria was in UK's throne.

Its founding is attributed to Thomas Davidson, a Scottish philosopher, and its early members included George Bernard Shaw, Sidney Webb, Annie Besant, Edward Pease, and Graham Wallas.
Shaw and Webb, later joined by Webb’s wife, Beatrice, were the outstanding leaders of the society for many years.
In 1889 the society published its best-known tract, Fabian Essays in Socialism, edited by Shaw. It was followed in 1952 by New Fabian Essays, edited by Richard H.S. Crossman.

The Fabians at first attempted to permeate the Liberal and Conservative parties with socialist ideas, but later they helped to organize the separate Labour Representation Committee, which became the Labour Party in 1906. The Fabian Society has since been affiliated with the Labour Party.

Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ১২) ‘The Canterbury Tales’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
The Canterbury Tales, frame story by Geoffrey Chaucer, written in Middle English in 1387–1400.
[Source: britannica]

English Literature.exp:
Literary Work : Important Characters

The Tempest : Prospero, Caliban, Ariel, Miranda, Ferdinand.

English Literature.exp:
‘Mosca’ is an important character in the play ‘Volpone’ by Ben Johnson.
Other important characters are: Volpone, Celia, Bonario, Corvino, Voltore.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১৫) ‘Achilles’ is an important character in -
English Literature.exp:
‘Achilles’ is an important character in The Iliad (Epic) by Homer.
Other important characters are: Hector, Agamemnon, Helen, Paris, Priam, Nestor, Briseis, Menelaus, Apollo, Athena, Thetis.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১৬) “Ignorance is not innocence but sin.” - this is a famous quotation by -
English Literature.exp:

Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১৭) “Oh, lift me as a wave, a leaf, a cloud! I fall upon the thorns of life.” - this quotation is collected from -
English Literature.option4: ঘ) Ode to the West Wind
English Literature.exp:
Some important quotations from ‘Ode to the west wind’ by P. B Shelley:
- If winter comes can spring be far behind.
- Oh, lift me as a wave, a leaf, a cloud! I fall upon the thorns of life.
- Wild Spirit, which art moving everywhere; Destroyer and preserver; hear, O hear!
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১৮) “Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.” this is a quotation by -
English Literature.exp:
“Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.”- is an important quotation by Rousseau.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ১৯) Which one is the first English long poem?
English Literature.exp:
Beowulf is the first English long poem (the earliest epic). The Author of Beowulf is Anonymous.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ২০) Who is the writer of Christ?
English Literature.exp:
- Cynewulf known as The writer of Christ.
- Caedmon – ইংরেজি সাহিত্যের প্রথম কবি হিসেবে পরিচিত। Fathers of English Sacred Songs.
- John Wycliffe - Father of English prose.
Translated Bible / New Testament into English prose.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ২১) The Age of Chaucer exist from -
English Literature.exp:
The Middle English Period
I) Anglo-Norman Period (1066 – 1340)
II) Age of Chaucer (1340 – 1400)
III) Barren Age (1400 – 1485)
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ২২) Who translated The Bible into English?
English Literature.exp:
John Wycliffe (1324-84) is called the Father of English prose. He translated The Bible into English from Latin.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৩) Who is known as ‘Wonderful Teacher’?
English Literature.exp:
Roger Bacon, byname Doctor Mirabilis (Latin: “Wonderful Teacher”), (born c. 1220, Ilchester, Somerset, or Bisley, Gloucester, England — died 1292 in Oxford, English Franciscan philosopher and educational reformer who was a major medieval proponent of experimental science.
Bacon studied mathematics, astronomy, optics, alchemy, and languages. He was the first European to describe in detail the process of making gunpowder, and he proposed flying machines and motorized ships and carriages.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ২৪) Who is considered as the father of English Modern Poetry?
English Literature.exp:
Geoffrey Chaucer is the Father of English Modern Poetry. His best writing is Canterbury Tales.
He is also called -
- Father of English Language,
- Father of English literature,
First Humourist in English Literature,
The First great Modernist.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ২৫) ‘The Golden Targe’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
‘The Golden Targe’ was written by William Dunbar. Which wears its allegory very lightly and charms with descriptive imagery.
Source: Britannica.

English Literature.question: ২৬) Robert Henryson was a/an ____ author.
English Literature.exp:
Robert Henryson, Scottish poet, the finest of early fabulists in Britain. He is described on some early title pages as schoolmaster of Dunfermline—probably at the Benedictine abbey school—and he appears among the dead poets in William Dunbar’s Lament for the Makaris, which was printed about 1508.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ২৭) The drama ‘Macbeth’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
William Shakespeare was an English dramatist and poet of the sixteenth century. He is known mostly for his plays.
His famous Tragedies are Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Romeo and Juliet, Antony and Cleopatra, Titus Andronicus, Timon of Athens.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ২৮) Which literary work was written by John Dryden?
English Literature.exp:
John Dryden is the Father of Modern English Criticism.
His famous works are All for Love, The Indian Emperor, Aureng-Zebe, The Mistaken Husband, Absalom and Achitophel, MacFlecknoe, The essay of Dramatic Poesy, The Conquest of Granada, The Medal of John Bays.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

English Literature.question: ২৯) ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Much Ado About Nothing, comedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, written probably in 1598–99 and printed in a quarto edition from the author’s own manuscript in 1600.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩০) ‘Antony and Cleopatra’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
Shakespeare's Tragedy: Julius Caesar (1599), Antony and Cleopatra (1606), Titus Andronicus, Romeo and Juliet (1594), Hamlet (1601), Troilus and Cressida, Othello (1604), Macbeth (1605), King lear (1605). Timon of Athens.
The Tempest is a comedy.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৩১) Who is called the poet of poets in English Literature?
English Literature.exp:
Edmund Spenser is known as the 'Poet of Poets' in English literature. His famous Epic is The Faerie Queene.
His famous books - The Shepherds Calendar, The Ruins of Time, Amoretti (Collection of 89 Sonnets).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৩২) ‘Doctor Faustus’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Christopher Marlowe is the poet of Elizabethan Period. His famous Tragedy are Doctor Faustus, The Jew of Malta, Tamburlaine the Great, Edward II, The Massacre of Paris etc.
The Passionate Shepherd to His Love and Hero and Leander are the Lyrics of Christopher Marlowe.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৩৩) Who is not a University Wits?
English Literature.exp:
University Wits:
Elizabethan Period - এর একদল নাট্যকার (Dramatist) - কে একত্রে University Wits বলা হয়।
এই নাট্যকারদের প্রায় সবাই Oxford বা Cambridge University এর গ্রাজুয়েট।
তারা তাদের লেখনীতে গতানুগতিক ধারা পরিহার করে বৈচিত্র্য ও সমসাময়িক আধুনিকতা আনায়ন করেন।

University Wits - রা হচ্ছেনঃ
1. Christopher Marlowe - (Cambridge)
2. Robert Greene - (Cambridge)
3. Thomas Nashe - (Cambridge)
4. Thomas Lodge - (Oxford)
5. George Peele- (Oxford)
6. John Lyly - (Oxford)
7. Thomas Kyd (not university-trained)

University Wits - দের মধ্যে Christopher Marlowe কে Father of Tragedy বলা হয়।
তিনি Blank Verse উন্নতি ঘটান যা প্রায় পরবর্তী ৫০ বছর পর্যন্ত English Theatre কে নতুন ধারা তৈরি করে দেয়।

উৎসঃ এনসিক্লোপিডিয়া ব্রিটানিকা ও An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman।

English Literature.question: ৩৪) ‘Volpone’ is a play written by -
English Literature.exp:
Volpone, in full Volpone; or, The Fox, comedy in five acts by Ben Jonson, performed about 1605/06 and published in 1607.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৫) Who wrote ‘The Spanish Tragedy’?
English Literature.exp:
“The Spanish Tragedy” is written by Thomas Kyd. Thomas Kyd, English dramatist who, with his The Spanish Tragedy (sometimes called Hieronimo, or Jeronimo, after its protagonist), initiated the revenge tragedy of his day.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৬) ‘The Good Morrow’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
John Donne is The Father of Metaphysical Poets.
He is called the Poet of Love and Religious Poet.
His famous poems are: The Good Morrow, The Sun Rising, The Canonization, Twicknam Garden, For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Anatomy of the World (book), The Frea, The Ecstasy, The Funeral etc.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৭) ‘Paradise Lost’ is ____ by John Milton.
English Literature.exp:
John Milton is a writer of Caroline Age. He is called Epic Poet and also called 'A great master of verse in Puritan Period'.
His famous Epics are Paradise Lost and Paradise Regained.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৮) ‘Holy living’ is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
Jeremy Taylor’s major works are –
- The Rule and Exercises of Holy Living (1650), a sermon in prose.
- The Rule and Exercises of Holy Dying (1651), a sermon in prose.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৯) Hudibras, a satire in verse was written by -
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Butler is the writer of the Restoration Period. His famous satire in verse is Hudibras.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪০) Who was known as the ''Father of Modern English Criticism''?
English Literature.exp:
John Dryden is the Father of Modern English Criticism.
His famous works are All for Love, The Indian Emperor, Aureng-Zebe, The Mistaken Husband, Absalom and Achitophel, MacFlecknoe, The essay of Dramatic Poesy, The Conquest of Granada, The Medal of John Bays.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

English Literature.question: ৪১) ‘The Rape of the Lock’ is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
The Rape of the Lock, mock-epic poem in heroic couplets by Alexander Pope. The first version, published in 1712, consisted of two cantos; the final version, published in 1714, was expanded to five cantos. Based on an actual incident and written to reconcile the families that had been estranged by it, The Rape of the Lock recounts the story of a young woman named Belinda who has a lock of hair stolen by an ardent young man.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৪২) “To err is human, to forgive is divine” is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Alexander Pope is a Mock Heroic Poet.
His famous quotations are-
-'Fools rush in where angels fear to tread'
-'An honest man is the noblest work of God'
-'To err is human, to forgive is divine'
-'A little learning is a dangerous thing'.
[Source: An Essay on Criticism by Alexander Pope, Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৪৩) How many voyages exist in ‘Gulliver’s Travels’?
English Literature.exp:
Jonathon Swift ইংরেজি সাহিত্যের একজন বিখ্যাত বিদ্রূপাত্মক সাহিত্য রচয়িতা। তাকে Misanthropist বা মনুষ্যদ্বেষী বলা হয়। ‘Gulliver’s Travels’ তার বিখ্যাত সাহিত্য, যা প্রকাশিত হয় ২৮ অক্টোবর, ১৭২৬ সালে। ‘Gulliver’s Travels’ চারটি খন্ডে বিভক্তঃ A voyage to Lilliput, A voyage to Brobdingnag, A voyage to Balnibarbi, A voyage to the country of Houyhnhnms.
Source: Live MCQ Archive

English Literature.question: ৪৪) ‘Captain Hercules Vinegar’ is the pen name of -
English Literature.exp:
Henry Fielding is regarded as the 'Father of Modern English Novel'.
He is famous for Picaresque Novels.
His pen name is Captain Hercules Vinegar.
His famous plays are: Rape Upon Rape, The Temple Beau, The Tragedy of Tragedies, The Modern Husband and his famous Novels are Tom Jones, Amelia, Joseph Andrews.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৪৫) Samuel Johnson is a writer from -
English Literature.exp:
Dr. Samuel Johnson is a writer from The Age of Sensibility (1745–1798). This is also called The Age of Johnson.
Dr. Samuel Johnson works: - Dictionary (1755),
- The History of Rasselas,
- Prince of Abyssinia (1759),
- Preface to Shakespeare (1765).
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৬) Who has written the poem “Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard”?
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Gray is famous for Graveyard Poet. His famous Elegy is 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'. His other notable works are Alexander’s Feast, Ode to adversity, The Bard.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৪৭) Which one was written by Samuel Richardson?
English Literature.exp:
Pamela, in full Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded, novel in epistolary style by Samuel Richardson, published in 1740 and based on a story about a servant and the man who, failing to seduce her, marries her. Pamela is often credited with being the first English novel. Although the validity of this claim depends on the definition of the term novel, Richardson was clearly innovative in his concentration on a single action.
Source: britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪৮) The Literary term ‘euphemism’ means -
English Literature.exp:
Euphemism: সুভাষণ
Inoffensive expression: শালীন অভিব্যক্তি
Source: Bangla Academy Dictionary- English to Bangla

English Literature.question: ৪৯) Using the literary term ‘irony’ the author means -
English Literature.option1: ক) The indirect meaning of a word
English Literature.option2: খ) the opposite of the surface meaning
English Literature.option4: ঘ) A story of double meaning
English Literature.exp:
Irony:
a situation in which something which was intended to have a particular result has the opposite or a very different result
Source: Cambridge Dictionary

English Literature.question: ৫০) What is Limerick?
English Literature.option1: ক) a humorous poem with five lines
English Literature.option2: খ) A form of one-act play
English Literature.exp:
Limerick is a humorous poem with five lines, the first two lines having the same final sound as the last line.
Source: Cambridge Dictionary
